key_insight: Low-dimensional perovskite capping increases surface roughness while preserving—and improving—electronic uniformity in 3D perovskite films.
engineering_relevance: Separating electronic quality from surface smoothness offers a design route toward more durable perovskite photovoltaics.
method: Cap 3D perovskites with Ruddlesden–Popper layers derived from 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium.
Compare statistical AFM topography with spatially resolved photoluminescence and quasi-Fermi level splitting.
Evaluate pristine and capped films under accelerated aging.
evidence_signal: Despite increased roughness, capped films showed enhanced photoluminescence, reduced non-radiative recombination, and more uniform radiative quasi-Fermi level splitting, retaining greater optoelectronic homogeneity during aging.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative effect sizes or device-level efficiency and lifetime results, so photovoltaic performance gains remain unverified here.
paper_title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures
